_design_note: The opponent-shaping arm. Its only difference from F2 is reward_version A06 -> A07, which adds one term to the potential and leaves every event weight and the death penalty byte-identical. Motivated by a measurement, not a story: scripts/diagnose_kill_opportunities.py replayed F2 over 900 tournament rounds and found it standing 9,930 times where a bomb would have caught an opponent, able to escape after dropping in 97.9 percent of those, and dropping in 8.0 percent. On rule_based_agent's own trigger -- an opponent within one step -- it dropped 218 times out of 3,299. The agent reaches the position and declines the bomb, so this is a decision problem and shaping the decision has a target. Counting training events explains why it cannot fix itself: F2 saw 820 KILLED_OPPONENT against 156,870 COIN_COLLECTED, so the largest weight in the table carries 1.7 percent of the positive reward mass.

_predeclared_design_numbers.changed_factor: reward_version A06 -> A07 (shaping potential_v1 -> potential_v2); the event table and death penalty are identical, so the new term is the only variable
_predeclared_design_numbers.control: runs/m3_f2_wide_ddqn_5000_vs3rb_20260827/ -- repeat-measured tournament score 2.5396 (sd 0.121 over ten repeats), coins_share 0.2548, kills 0.0556/round, survival 14.3%
_predeclared_design_numbers.falsification: Take-up unchanged means the shaping term does not reach the decision and the kill gap is not closable this way; record the negative result and stop.
_predeclared_design_numbers.prediction: None stated. Five mechanism hypotheses were overturned by measurement this round.
_predeclared_design_numbers.reporting: All five training-seed distributions, coins_share, kills, the death split, the take-up numbers, and the ten repeat measurements individually.
_predeclared_design_numbers.resolution_tournament: Section 7.26.3: one measurement settles nothing. Repeat the classic_versus_opponents suite ten times against F2's ten.
_predeclared_design_numbers.the_cost_to_watch: F2 already loses 42.1 percent of its deaths to opponents against M3.4's 34.0. Pushing it toward opponents is expected to raise that; report the death split and the survival rate next to the score, and treat a score gain bought with a survival collapse the way section 7.25.3 treated M3.13's.
_predeclared_design_numbers.the_metric_that_decides_it: Re-run diagnose_kill_opportunities.py. The number that has to move is the 8.0 percent take-up of blast-covering positions, and the 6.6 percent on rule_based's adjacency trigger. Tournament score moving without those moving would not be this term working.
_predeclared_design_numbers.why_it_cannot_corrupt_the_objective: potential-based shaping is policy-invariant (Ng, Harada & Russell 1999). If declining the bomb is genuinely optimal, A07 cannot teach otherwise; it can only speed up learning the 5.0 that KILLED_OPPONENT already carries.
